about: Techniques made real in this repo. Every entry's numbers carry status: real-measured / derived-from-measured / assumption / not-measured, plus how they were computed and the sample size. Counterpart to training/NOT_RUN_HERE.json, which records the techniques that were NOT run here.
rules: No number is written by hand. Everything below was produced by the command named in its entry.
A value that cannot be measured on a laptop is marked `assumption` or `not-measured`. It is never given a plausible-looking default.
Null and negative results are recorded with the same prominence as positive ones.

techniques.name: MLE search agent over the ranking config space
techniques.headline: Best config v32 (rrf_k: 20 -> 40) led on dev by +0.00090, but on the sealed test split the delta is +0.00167 with CI95 [-0.00134, 0.00504], which straddles zero. That is a null result: the search found no config that is measurably better than v4.

trials.how: each trial registered a real model version via search-svc POST /models/candidate and ran search-svc POST /eval/compare on the dev split

usd_spent.how: measured wall clock per trial x $0.0017/CPU-min (rate: assumption, minutes: measured)
usd_spent.caveat: search-svc memoises per-query eval results by config hash, so re-running a search that revisits the same configs costs a fraction of the first, cold run. Quote the cold number.

best_observed_dev_delta.how: paired per-query NDCG@10 delta vs champion, percentile bootstrap 1000 resamples

sealed_holdout_delta.how: the test split was never scored during the search; the winner was scored on it once

leaderboard_guard.note: no trial was scored on 'test'; only the winning config is, once, after the budget closes

techniques.honest_note: a null result. Nothing here proposes a promotion.

techniques.name: Adaptive red-team attacker agent
techniques.command: ops_mcp.tools.run_red_team(generations=8, per_generation=16, usd_cap=1.0)  [seed 20260915 here for reproducibility]

attempts.how: attack strings composed at run time and fired at shop_mcp.injection.detect_injection, the guard shop-mcp really runs on untrusted seller text; de-duplicated

usd_spent.how: measured CPU time x $0.0017/CPU-min. The attacker is a local evolutionary search, so no LLM tokens were bought; the $1 cap was never approached.

regression_suite_block_rate.how: the seed suite in evals/tasks.yaml, which is the eval gate's metric

open_findings_still_bypassing.how: every past bypass is replayed against the CURRENT detector

techniques.honest_note: A zero attack-success rate here is evidence about THIS budget and THIS operator set only. It is not proof the pipeline cannot be injected.

techniques.name: Model routing / cascade with route receipts

requests_made.how: every one a real HTTP POST /search to search-svc, timed in the BFF

cost_per_1k_always_premium.how: the same queries driven through the premium arm alone, paired control

claude_arm.how: no Claude CLI runs were recorded in the measured process, so no LLM-arm latency or cost is claimed. metrics.ts returns null and the router says so.

usd_per_cpu_min.how: laptop CPU rate. The wall-clock ms it multiplies are measured; this rate is not.

techniques.honest_note: the cascade as configured LOSES money on this traffic: the rank1/rank3 margin threshold fires on almost every query, so the router pays for both arms. Pure routing without the cascade is the arm that saves. Both numbers are reported; neither was tuned to look good.
techniques.not_measured: quality per arm. This reports cost and latency only; NDCG@10 per mode is search-svc /eval/ndcg's job.

techniques.name: LLM online evals + OpenTelemetry GenAI tracing
techniques.command: OTEL_ENABLED=1 npm run dev:bff; GET /api/ops/router; POST /api/ops/online-evals/export; GET /api/ops/online-evals/agreement

sessions_ingested_this_run.how: sessions the BFF actually served, one per traced routed request

sessions_sampled.how: deterministic: hash(trace_id) < 1.0; re-running picks the same sessions

pairs_with_ground_truth.how: held-out ESCI qrels (dev+test); E/S = relevant, C/I = not

tracing.conventions: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (Development status); names isolated in bff/src/otel.ts ATTR

judge.why: the ranker is a bi-encoder + cross-encoder; the judge is lexical, so it is not scoring its own output. A same-family judge is the self-preference bias arXiv:2410.21819 documents.
judge.limits: a lexical judge cannot see semantics; it will call a correct substitute irrelevant. Its measured agreement with ESCI gold below is the honest ceiling on what it can tell you.

techniques.sample_size_caveat: n = 244 labelled pairs. Every figure above is conditioned on that. A kappa from a few hundred pairs is an indication, not a certification; the playbook's own bar (29 US-1 AC2) is a kappa threshold agreed on a human gold set, which does not exist here.
techniques.honest_note: the lexical online judge does NOT agree with ESCI gold beyond chance at this sample size - a negative kappa with a relevant base rate above 70% means a judge that always said 'relevant' would score higher. The judge is not fit to gate anything and is reported as such.

techniques.name: Cost-aware retrain triggers over measured inputs

current_p95_ms.how: 30 real search-svc POST /search calls (mode rrf_rerank, the champion path), round-trip timed in ops-mcp, 3 warm-up calls discarded; nearest-rank p95
current_p95_ms.caveat: laptop wall clock including HTTP round trip, so it is an upper bound on service-internal latency; a small sample makes the p95 coarse - the sample size is reported for exactly that reason

rebuild_cpu_min.how: wall clock around a real search-svc POST /models/candidate that rebuilds the champion's own config (encoder load, reranker warm, MLflow registration), priced at the stated $/CPU-min rate
rebuild_cpu_min.caveat: this laptop reuses data/embeddings.npy, so it does NOT include re-embedding the catalogue. A rebuild that changes the embedding model is a different, much larger number and is not claimed here.

rebuild_usd.how: measured CPU-minutes x the stated $/CPU-min rate

usd_per_cpu_min.how: ~$0.10 per vCPU-hour on demand. Stated, not measured.

value_usd_per_0.01_ndcg_day.how: set SPARKY_VALUE_USD_PER_001_NDCG_DAY to the business's own figure. It is revenue per NDCG point per day of traffic and cannot be derived from anything on this laptop: there is no revenue signal here.
value_usd_per_0.01_ndcg_day.never: no default is applied. With nothing supplied, ROI is reported as a break-even threshold and a sensitivity table instead of a single number.

break_even_example.how: at a hypothetical +0.005 NDCG gain and the measured rebuild cost: the $/day value of 0.01 NDCG at which the retrain exactly pays for itself. Needs no value assumption at all.

techniques.honest_note: the trigger currently DENIES every remediation, because the technique-16 search found no config measurably better than the champion. That denial is the correct output of a cost-aware policy and is not worked around.
